questions.q: Why would you export a PyTorch model to ONNX instead of leaving it as a pickle file?
options: ONNX trains models faster than PyTorch
ONNX is a framework-neutral format, so the model can be served by any ONNX-compatible runtime without the original framework installed
Pickle files cannot store neural network weights
ONNX automatically improves model accuracy
questions.explain: ONNX is a portable graph format usable across frameworks and languages, unlike pickle, which is Python- and library-version-sensitive.

questions.q: In a KServe InferenceService, what does the `storageUri` field point to?
options: A running Kubernetes pod
The location of the serialized model artifact in object storage
The GitHub repository containing the training code
A DNS record for the serving endpoint
questions.explain: storageUri tells KServe where to find the packaged model artifact (e.g. in S3) so it can launch the appropriate built-in server to load it.

questions.q: In SageMaker, what is the relationship between create_model, create_endpoint_config, and create_endpoint?
options: They are three interchangeable ways to do the exact same thing
create_model registers the artifact and container, create_endpoint_config defines hardware and traffic split, and create_endpoint stands up the running infrastructure
create_endpoint must be called before create_model
Only create_endpoint is ever required
questions.explain: The three calls are deliberately separate steps, which is what allows a new model/config to be prepared without touching the currently live endpoint.

questions.q: Why containerize a packaged model instead of just shipping the serialized file?
options: Containers make the model file smaller
So the exact runtime, library versions, and system dependencies travel with the model instead of depending on the target machine's setup
Containerizing is required by law for all ML models
It removes the need for a model server entirely
questions.explain: Containerizing bundles the runtime environment with the model artifact, avoiding 'works on my laptop' failures when it runs somewhere else.

questions.q: What does Seldon Core's `graph` field in a SeldonDeployment let you do that a simple KServe predictor spec does not?
options: Chain multiple components, like a preprocessor, the model, and an outlier detector, into one request path
Automatically retrain the model on a schedule
Store the model in a relational database
Skip the need for a container image entirely
questions.explain: Seldon's prediction graph is built to compose multiple components into a single serving pipeline, which is more flexible than a single built-in predictor.
